title: Quasi-identifier combining location data
description: Location pings contain quasi-identifying attributes (coordinates, timestamps) that can be combined with other data to identify individuals
assumptions: Location data is collected with user context that enables linking

title: Profiling individual through location history
description: Location history data can be analyzed to profile individual movement patterns, habits, and routines
assumptions: Location data is stored and accessible for analysis

title: Quasi-identifier in location data
description: Location pings contain combinations of attributes (coordinates, timestamps) that can uniquely identify individuals when combined with other data
assumptions: Location data is associated with user accounts or can be linked to individuals

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location data reveals sensitive attributes about individuals including whereabouts, routines, and potentially sensitive locations
assumptions: Location data is processed and stored

title: Sensitive data type collected
description: Location data is considered sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required
assumptions: Location tracking is implemented in the mobile app

title: Excessive amount of location data processed
description: Continuous location pings may result in excessive volume of personal data beyond functional necessity
assumptions: Location pings are collected at high frequency

title: Excessive data retention
description: Location history may be stored longer than functionally needed for the app's purpose
assumptions: Location data is persisted in the store without clear retention policies

title: Unawareness of location processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location data is being collected, stored, and processed
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate location tracking extent

title: Lack of control over location preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences for location data collection frequency and scope
assumptions: Granular consent controls for location tracking are not implemented

title: Lack of control over data erasure
description: Users may not be able to easily rectify or erase their location history data
assumptions: No user interface for managing or deleting location history

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Location data may be collected and processed beyond what is actually needed for the app's functionality
assumptions: Location tracking is not strictly necessary for core app features

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Location data may be stored longer than necessary for the functional purpose
assumptions: No clear retention policy or automatic deletion mechanism

title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's live location data can be linked to a specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking and association of location data with individual identity.
assumptions: Location data is associated with identifiable user accounts or devices

title: Profiling an individual through location data
description: Live location data can be analyzed to profile a child's movements, routines, and patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily activities and whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data is collected over time and can be analyzed for patterns

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system processes identified personal data (child's live location) which directly reveals the identity and whereabouts of the data subject.
assumptions: Location data is tied to identifiable individuals

title: Data Propagation to External Analytics Partner
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics are propagated from the mobile app backend to an external advertising/analytics partner (EE4) beyond what may be functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The analytics partner may use this data for purposes beyond funding the free tier, such as building user profiles or selling data.

title: Predetermined External Data Recipient
description: Personal data is shared with a predetermined set of external parties (advertising/analytics partner) that may not be functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The advertising partner is a known third party that may have its own data processing policies.

title: User Unawareness of Data Sharing
description: Data subjects (app users) may not be aware that their usage and engagement analytics are being shared with external advertising/analytics partners to fund the free tier.
assumptions: Privacy policies may not clearly communicate this data sharing, or users may not read them.

title: Lack of User Control Over Data Sharing
description: Users may lack control to opt-out of analytics data sharing with the advertising partner, as this is tied to funding the free tier.
assumptions: The app may not provide granular consent options for this specific data flow.

title: Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics may contain more personal data than is actually needed to fund the app's free tier, violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: The analytics data may include more granular information than strictly necessary for the stated purpose.

title: Potential Invalid Consent for Data Sharing
description: Data sharing with the advertising partner may rely on consent that is not freely given, specifically conditioned on receiving the free tier service (bundled consent).
assumptions: Users may feel compelled to consent to analytics sharing to access the free app tier.

title: Quasi-Identifier Re-identification Risk
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., device IDs, usage patterns, timestamps) that could be combined with other data to re-identify individual users.
assumptions: Aggregation may not be sufficiently robust to prevent re-identification through data combination.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the actual aggregation methodology and data granularity.

title: Quasi-identifiers in Analytics Data
description: The aggregated analytics data may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., usage frequency, app features used, time spent) that are unique to individual data subjects.
assumptions: Even aggregated data can contain quasi-identifiers that enable identification when combined with external data.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific attributes included in the analytics.
